_authority: Laws L12 and L13 in enforceable form: what motion is allowed, what it must declare, and what is rejected by name. SKILL.md carries the law; this file carries the mechanics and the reject list. scripts/check_visuals.py reads the vocabularies below.
_owner_note: course-visuals is the owning skill for L12 (asset provenance) and L13 (animation must explain a mechanism). Before this file they had no owner and depended on a plugin-root CLAUDE.md that Claude Code does not load.

categories._rule: Every animation in a course declares exactly one category. An animation that cannot be categorised is not built.

teaching.means: the motion IS the content - it shows a change the learner must understand
requires: learner or instructor control - play, pause, step, replay
a caption per step saying what changed and why
no autoplay that runs past the point being made
a resting state that is readable with the animation stopped
teaching.gate: must answer the four questions before it is built

affordance.means: motion that teaches the INTERACTION, not the content - a tap hint on a first-use control
requires: it stops once the learner has interacted
it is not the only signal that a control exists
affordance.note: legitimate, and a different thing from teaching motion. Do not count it as instructional.

ambient.means: scene motion that makes an illustration read as a scene - drifting water, a slow vapour puff
requires: declared as ambient in the storyboard
it must not compete with a teaching animation on the same screen
it must not imply a process the learner might read as content
ambient.budget: at most one ambient effect per screen, and none on a screen that carries a teaching animation
ambient.honesty: if it cannot be described as ambient without embarrassment, it is decoration - remove it

chrome.means: interface transitions - a panel opening, a card settling, a progress dot filling
chrome.owner: course-module-ui and course-module-ux own chrome motion; it is out of scope here
chrome.note: listed so a review does not mistake chrome for content

four_questions._rule: Every substantial animation answers all four IN THE STORYBOARD, before implementation. An animation that cannot answer them is decoration with a budget.
four_questions.q4: What should the learner understand afterwards, that they did not before?
four_questions.failure_signature: If q4 can be answered by the caption alone, with the motion removed, the motion is not carrying the teaching. Ship the caption and a static figure.

rejected_patterns._note: Named so a review can point at the name instead of arguing about taste. Each is rejected because it moves without explaining.
rejected_patterns.random_floating: elements drifting with no referent - nothing in the subject is floating
rejected_patterns.decorative_pulsing: a glow or scale loop on something that is not changing state
rejected_patterns.bouncing_icons: attention-seeking motion on a static concept
rejected_patterns.unnecessary_fade_sequences: content fading in on load because it looked flat - this delays reading and teaches nothing
rejected_patterns.moving_arrows_without_process: an arrow animating along a path where no process was explained; motion asserting a flow the screen never established
rejected_patterns.meaningless_autoplay_loops: a loop that restarts forever, so the learner cannot tell where the sequence begins or ends
rejected_patterns.animation_because_animation_was_requeste: motion added to satisfy a request for animation rather than a learning need. The correct response to 'add an animation' is to find the state change worth animating - or to say there is not one.
rejected_patterns.parallax_and_scroll_reveal: motion driven by scrolling rather than by the content's own logic
rejected_patterns.spinning_loaders_on_local_content: everything is packaged locally and loads instantly; a spinner invents a wait

decorative_vocabulary._use: scripts/check_visuals.py flags a CSS @keyframes or animation-name matching these when it is infinite and has no motion declaration. A match is a QUESTION, not proof - the script warns, a human decides.

teaching_vocabulary._use: these names, and a motion declaration, are what a teaching animation looks like in the markup

motion_declaration._rule: Any element carrying a non-chrome animation declares its category in the markup, so a static check and a human review can both see the author's intent.
motion_declaration.on_a_teaching_animation: also carry data-step on each revealed layer, and provide play/pause/step/replay controls
motion_declaration.why: without a declaration, a reviewer cannot distinguish a deliberate ambient puff from a decorative pulse somebody added to fill a screen - and neither can a script

accessibility_and_tablet.reduced_motion: any screen with an infinite animation must honour prefers-reduced-motion: reduce by stopping ambient motion. Teaching animation may remain, because it is content - but it must not autoplay under reduced motion.
accessibility_and_tablet.offscreen: animation pauses when its screen is not visible. A loop running behind a slide the class is not on burns battery and desynchronises a replay.
accessibility_and_tablet.no_hover: no animation may be triggered only by hover
